props.title: Not Another Teen Movie
props.initialSlug: Hilarious spoof mocks every teen movie cliché

sections.content: Not Another Teen Movie (2001) stands as the definitive parody of late 90s/early 2000s teen films, ruthlessly skewering classics like She's All That (1999), 10 Things I Hate About You (1999), and American Pie (1999). Chris Evans, in his breakout role as Jake Wyler, perfectly channels Freddie Prinze Jr.'s popular jock archetype, while Chyler Leigh's Janey Briggs ("the pretty ugly girl") mercilessly mocks Rachel Leigh Cook's paint-covered artist transformation. The film's genius lies in its hyper-aware commentary on teen movie tropes - from the wise black friend who only exists to give advice to the token foreign exchange student played deliberately over-the-top by Cerina Vincent.

sections.content: The late 90s teen movie renaissance kicked off with Clueless (1995), which modernized Jane Austen's Emma for Beverly Hills. This sparked a wave of literary adaptations including 10 Things I Hate About You (1999) and Cruel Intentions (1999), transforming classic literature into contemporary teen drama. These films established a formula that Not Another Teen Movie would later dissect: the makeover sequence, synchronized dance numbers, dramatic confessions at sporting events, and the "all-important" prom climax. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Teen Movie Parody

While Scary Movie (2000) had proven there was an appetite for direct genre parody, Not Another Teen Movie elevated the form through its encyclopedic knowledge of its source material. The film references everything from The Breakfast Club (1985) to Varsity Blues (1999), creating a meta-commentary on how formulaic teen films had become. This paved the way for later genre deconstructions like Easy A (2010), which both honored and questioned teen movie conventions while telling its own story.
